newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police risk death to raid drug fields.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police risk death to raid drug fields.

text.p: Mexican drug agents carried out a mission on Tuesday to wipe out marijuana and opium poppy fields in a remote region of this northern Mexican state.
Dozens of armed agents descended from helicopters and uprooted giant marijuana plants growing along a jagged set of mountains some 60 miles (100 km) southeast of the state capital, Culiacan.
Agents also kept an eye on nearby hills, where they have been shot at by angry marijuana and poppy farmers.
"They shoot at us when we aren't looking," said one agent, who wished not to be identified, as he hauled an armful of marijuana to a bonfire. "Some of our partners have died."
The agent also said local traffickers have shot down police helicopters used in raids.
His superior, Norma Martinez, a delegate from Mexico's National Institute for Combatting Drugs, denied that agents were killed or helicopters were shot down.
Green patches of marijuana decorate the hills of this arid state, marking a spot for the police to land. If the hills are too steep to allow a landing, helicopters spray chemicals.
Agents are moved around constantly, striking in one state one day and another the next. They are often away on a mission for to six months at a time before getting to see their families.
Officials say the raids are a visible part of Mexico's war on drugs, although they admit they are fighting a losing battle. Within a month, the field wiped out by agents is often replanted.
"There is year-round production; it never stops," said Gabriel Diaz Gonzalez, another drug agency delegate.
